plan.symptom: Hovering the "2,000+ Pre-made Designs" thumbnail packs (trios of images with large blue shadows) on the Divi gallery page makes their hover animation stutter badly — the reporter estimates "3 to 12 or 20 fps" instead of smooth 60fps, and on a Radeon R9 270 it sometimes skips the animation entirely and jumps to the end state. Straddles "animation" and "responsiveness" (the bug carries both perf keywords) since the jank is triggered by a hover interaction, but the complaint is explicitly about the animation not rendering smoothly, so it is classified as animation. Not a page-load bug, so no measurement was attempted.

root_cause.summary: The stutter is synchronous JPEG decoding on the content main thread, running inside WebRender display-list building on every animation frame. In the content process for elegantthemes.com (p-11 / t-62 GeckoMain), 428 of 649 active main-thread samples (65.9%) are under mozilla::image::Decoder::Decode, reached via DecodePool::SyncRunIfPossible from nsDisplayImage::CreateWebRenderCommands → RasterImage::GetImageProvider → LookupFrame → Decode. Style and layout are not the problem: RestyleManager::ProcessPendingRestyles is 31 samples (4.8%), Reflow markers average 217µs. The same "WrDisplayList" work costs 0.36–0.88ms when nothing is animating (20 markers, avg 0.56ms) and 5.2–42.4ms while a pack is hovered (49 markers, avg 19.8ms) — a 35x average / ~48x peak jump — and 94.5% of that inflated time is inside the Image Paint markers, i.e. inside RasterImage::GetImageProvider. The Divi hover transition animates `width`, `height` and `transform` on these thumbnails (visible in the CSS transition marker payloads), so the destination rect nsLayoutUtils::ComputeImageContainerDrawingParameters feeds to GetImageProvider changes every frame; downscale-during-decode makes the SurfaceCache key the destination size, so every frame misses and re-decodes the same large progressive JPEGs from scratch, synchronously, under FLAG_SYNC_DECODE. Roughly 3 images are re-decoded per frame at ~6ms each, and the two hovered trios (pack-6-1/2/3 and pack-8-3/4/5 in one frame at t=781ms) account for 35.2ms of a 36.8ms display-list build.
root_cause.hot_path: nsRefreshDriver::Tick → nsLayoutUtils::PaintFrame → nsDisplayList::PaintRoot → layers::EndTransactionWithoutLayer → BuildWebRenderCommands → nsDisplayTransform::CreateWebRenderCommands → nsDisplayImage::CreateWebRenderCommands → RasterImage::GetImageProvider → RasterImage::LookupFrame → RasterImage::Decode → LaunchDecodingTask → DecodePool::SyncRunIfPossible → image::Decoder::Decode (nsJPEGDecoder). Marker: "WrDisplayList" (avg 19.8ms / max 42.4ms while animating), with "Image Paint" markers of 3.8–16.4ms nested inside it.
root_cause.evidence:
Profile: Firefox 113 nightly, Windows 11, Ryzen 7 5800U, 2.841s, 1ms nominal interval (1625 samples on t-62 → ~1.75ms effective, so sample counts are proportional not absolute; absolute figures below come from markers).

Where the CPU is (content process p-11, t-62 GeckoMain, 1207.6ms process CPU = 88% of the 1367ms process total; 649 active samples):
- nsRefreshDriver::Tick 611 (94.1%) → Paint/nsLayoutUtils::PaintFrame 534 (82.3%) → nsDisplayList::PaintRoot 503 (77.5%) → EndTransactionWithoutLayer 469 (72.3%) → BuildWebRenderCommands 467 (72.0%) → CreateWebRenderCommandsFromDisplayList 466 (71.8%) → nsDisplayTransform::CreateWebRenderCommands 458 (70.6%) → nsDisplayImage::CreateWebRenderCommands 445 (68.6%) → RasterImage::GetImageProvider 440 (67.8%) → RasterImage::LookupFrame 437 (67.3%) → RasterImage::Decode 432 (66.6%) → LaunchDecodingTask → DecodePool::SyncRunIfPossible 429 (66.1%) → Decoder::Decode 428 (65.9%).
- Contrast: RestyleManager::ProcessPendingRestyles 31 (4.8%); SurfaceCache::Lookup only 4 (0.6%) — the cost is the miss, not the lookup.

Inside the decode (of 428):
- nsJPEGDecoder::OutputScanlines 240 (37.0%), of which ConvolutionFilter::ConvolveHorizontally 206 (31.7%) and skia::convolve_horizontally_sse2 151 self (23.3%) → downscale-during-decode is active, so decode size == destination size.
- jpeg_start_decompress 134 (20.6%) → consume_data 133, decode_mcu_AC_refine 63 (9.4% self), access_virt_barray, decode_mcu_DC_first → these are progressive JPEGs, so libjpeg must buffer whole-image coefficients before emitting a scanline.
- Decoder::AllocateFrame 30 (4.6%), incl. ClearSurface/memset 24 (3.7%) → a fresh surface allocated and zeroed per decode.

Marker evidence (absolute, on t-62):
- WrDisplayList, 69 total. Non-animating: 20 markers, min 360µs, avg 563µs, max 880µs. Animating: 49 markers, min 5.2ms, avg 19.76ms, max 42.38ms (≈968ms total).
- Image Paint (emitted by AutoProfilerImagePaintMarker in RasterImage::GetImageProvider, verified in searchfox): 2622 total, cleanly bimodal — 2470 under 1ms (1.2–50µs, cache hits) and 152 at 3.76–16.37ms, avg 6.018ms (≈915ms total, cache misses). No marker falls between 1ms and 3.76ms. 915ms of 968ms animating WrDisplayList time = 94.5%. 152 misses / 49 animating paints ≈ 3.1 sync decodes per frame.
- 15 distinct URLs sync-decoded, all elegantthemes.com/images/divi/layouts/pack-N-M-large.jpg; top: pack-5-4 54 samples, pack-6-3 53, pack-8-4 43, pack-8-3 38, pack-5-1 34. The same URL recurs on consecutive frames, e.g. pack-6-3-large.jpg re-decoded at t=945.6/959.7/973.9/1087/1106/1128/1141/1168/1184/1212/1256ms, 3.8–6.4ms each.
- One frame in full (RefreshDriverTick m-152, t=781.78ms, 40.04ms): style+reflow 1.5ms → ViewManagerFlush 37.7ms → DisplayList (Gecko DL build) 757µs → WrDisplayList 36.8ms, containing six long Image Paints — pack-6-1 7.72ms, pack-6-2 5.13ms, pack-8-3 5.87ms, pack-8-5 5.74ms, pack-6-3 5.30ms, pack-8-4 5.45ms = 35.2ms (96% of the WrDisplayList) — plus ~30 sub-4µs Image Paints for the non-animating thumbnails.
- CSS transition markers on the animating elements list `width`, `height`, `transform`, `left`, `right`, `opacity`, `color`, all 297–300ms long (145 markers, avg 277ms).
- 7 Jank markers, 52.2–80.7ms each (t=440ms, 473ms, 540ms, 757ms, 823ms, 1.223s, 1.940s).
- Frame cadence: idle RefreshDriverTicks are 16.67ms apart (60Hz). During the hover the ticks run 9–45.6ms and the gaps between successive paints reach 33–45ms in the worst stretches (m-201→m-190→m-202→m-193 at 465/498/543/582ms; m-211→m-212→m-213 at 785/825/869ms) ≈ 22–30fps. Main-thread CPU is 80% busy over 323ms–1.442s and 1.757s–2.092s.

Not the bottleneck on this machine — GPU process p-12: Renderer t-74 "Composite #2" 99 markers, avg 5.85ms, max 9.17ms (all under the 16.7ms budget); WRRenderBackend#2 t-89 BuildFrame 97 markers avg 3.35ms max 5.76ms, Batching avg 480µs. Texture uploads 52 markers avg 734µs. So the frame pipeline downstream of the content process keeps up; the content main thread is what misses vsync.

Scale: against the 16.7ms/60fps reference the worst frames are ~2.7x over budget (45.6ms tick). Against the profile's own baseline the same display-list build inflates 35x (0.56ms → 19.8ms) to 48x (0.88ms → 42.4ms). The large internal ratio is what pointed at operation count rather than frame cost, and the profile bears that out: the work is not merely slow, the same JPEGs are being fully re-decoded every frame.
root_cause.caveats:
Observed vs inferred:
- OBSERVED: the sample counts, the call chain from nsRefreshDriver::Tick down to Decoder::Decode, the DecodePool::SyncRunIfPossible label frame with its per-URL payloads, all marker names and durations, the bimodal Image Paint distribution, the CSS transition property list, and the GPU-side composite/BuildFrame timings.
- INFERRED (validated by reading mozilla-central, not measured): that the per-frame cache miss is caused by the animated destination size changing the SurfaceCache key. RasterImage::LookupFrame keys on `CanDownscaleDuringDecode(aSize) ? aSize : mSize`, and nsDisplayImage::CreateWebRenderCommands derives decodeSize from GetDestRect() via nsLayoutUtils::ComputeImageContainerDrawingParameters — so animating width/height changes the key. But the profile carries no surface sizes, so I never directly observed two different decode sizes for one image. An alternative or additional mechanism I cannot exclude is SurfaceCache eviction pressure: ~6 large surfaces re-decoded per frame for ~1.4s could be thrashing the cache, which would produce the same misses even at a stable size. Distinguishing them needs a capture with the SurfaceCache/imagelib logging or a run with image.downscale-during-decode.enabled=false.
- HYPOTHESIS, unvalidated: why FLAG_SYNC_DECODE is set at all. Reaching DecodePool::SyncRunIfPossible (rather than SyncRunIfPreferred) proves the flag is set, but the profile cannot say whether it comes from nsDisplayListBuilder::mSyncDecodeImages, nsImageFrame::mForceSyncDecoding, or `image-decoding: sync`. That matters for the fix: if the decode were async the main thread would not block, even if the redundant decoding remained.

Capture limitations:
- The recording's thread filter was "GeckoMain, Compositor, Renderer, SwComposite, RenderBackend, SceneBuilder, WrWorker, CanvasWorkers, DOM Worker, TaskController" — ImgDecoder threads were NOT recorded. I therefore cannot show that the decode pool was idle while the main thread decoded, only that the main thread did the decoding.
- Effective sampling was ~1.75ms, not the nominal 1ms (1625 samples over 2.841s), so sample counts understate absolute time; I used marker durations for all absolute figures and samples only for proportions.
- I read source from current mozilla-central via searchfox; the profile is Firefox 113 (March 2023, rev e86d4f07). The functions and flag plumbing still line up with the symbols in the profile, but the exact source lines quoted are not the build that was profiled.
- Source-level attribution stops at the frames: I did not read the Divi page's CSS/JS, so "the hover transition animates width/height" comes from the CSS transition marker payloads, not from the site's stylesheet.

What this does not explain:
- The reporter's specific numbers. On this machine (Ryzen 7 5800U, integrated Radeon) the worst frame intervals are 33–45ms, i.e. 22–30fps, not the reported 3–12fps. This capture is on different hardware and shows the same mechanism at a milder severity; I did not and cannot verify the reporter's figures from it.
- The "skips the animation entirely and jumps to the end state" symptom on a Radeon R9 270. Nothing in this profile shows a dropped or short-circuited transition, and this capture's GPU side is comfortably within budget (composites 5.9ms avg), so that part of the report may have a separate cause on that hardware.
- Whether this is a regression, and from what. The profile is a single capture with no comparison point.
